# Campaign bench — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (HTML + /640png). Do not edit mid-round.
# First 8: TARGET=/640png (tune_serial_loop sets AGENT_JMR_PNG=1). Last 4: full HTML media.
# Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-8bit-MTP · --max-iters 3 · VLM off.
Build a Dig Dug game. Dig tunnels four ways; pump monsters with harpoon or drop rocks. Digger: idle/dig/pump frames; monsters: walk + inflate frames — all pixel maps. Controls: Arrows, Space pump, R restart. Clear monsters to advance. Layered soil colors. On-screen sizes: digger/monsters ~40x40 (one soil tile; 16x10 tile field + HUD). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Digger move speed is classic-arcade brisk-but-readable (~2–3 tiles/s), not a blur. TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.
Build a Frogger game. Cross road then river to home slots. Frog: idle + mid-hop pixel-map frames per facing. Cars/trucks/logs/turtles as distinct pixel sprites. Controls: Arrows hop one cell per keydown edge, R restart. Fill homes to win; traffic/water/timeout loses a life. HUD score/lives/timer. On-screen sizes: frog ~40x40 (lane height 40), vehicles ~64x32, logs ~128x32. imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Start with 3 lives; HUD lives must equal state.lives; each death loses exactly one life. TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.
Build a Zelda-like top-down action RPG. Tile overworld; sword; NPCs; hearts. Hero poses (≥2 frames): idle/walk ×4 facings, sword, hit — pixel maps. Controls: Arrows, Z/Space sword, Enter talk, R restart. NO video — intro text crawl optional. Camera room-to-room. On-screen sizes: hero ~40x40, enemies/NPCs ~40x40 (one 40px tile). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Spawn goblins/enemies on the overworld to fight; draw Controls (Arrows, Z/Space sword, Enter talk, R). Left walk flips the right-facing walk frames. TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.
Build a Centipede game. Fixed shooter: blaster in the lower zone fires upward (muzzle points up). Centipede = head + body + tail as one chain (history trail). Shot middle splits; head scores most; hit leaves a mushroom. Blaster idle+fire frames; head/body pixel-map sprites. On-screen sizes: segments/mushrooms ~32x32 (20 columns), blaster ~48x48. Controls: Arrows move, Space fire, R restart. Clear wave to advance; segment or spider touch loses a life. HUD score/lives. imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Scatter mushrooms across the whole mushroom field (not only the top rows). Death is a brief flash — never leave the screen solid red. TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.
Build a Battlezone game. FIRST-PERSON 3D wireframe vector tank combat drawn with 2D canvas strokes (NOT three.js, NOT sprites, NOT top-down): wireframe mountains and a ground grid recede toward a horizon, player tank/turret outline in the lower view, enemy tanks approach and shoot back, radar/minimap in the corner. Controls: Arrows drive/turn, Space fire, R restart. Bright vector strokes on black. On-screen sizes: vector primary; any HUD icons ~32x32. imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Space MUST fire a vector shot along turret yaw. ArrowUp drives forward into the view; if motion feels reversed, use +cos on z (not three.js -cos). TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.
Build a Pac-Man game. Yellow chomping hero eats dots in a walled maze; four colored ghosts with distinct chase flavors. Hero: animated chomp frames facing move direction; ghosts: body + eyes toward movement; frightened blue frames. Four power-pellets frighten ghosts. Controls: Arrows (queued turns), R restart. Eat all dots to clear; ghost catch when not powered loses a life. COPY a compact connected maze template (tile coords). Expose dotsRemaining on window.state. Classic arcade silhouettes via pixel maps — not yellow circles. On-screen sizes: hero and ghosts ~40x40 (one maze tile; 16x11 tile maze fits the glass). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. COPY the connected starter maze; Pac-Man and ghosts stay on corridor tiles only. Ghosts are simple colored bodies+eyes (classic), not fancy multi-pose art. TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.

Colorful blocks with crisp pixel borders (small tile pixel maps or patterned fillRect tiles — not blank grey squares). HUD score/level/lines. On-screen sizes: blocks ~24x24 tiles. imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Build a Donkey Kong game. Single-screen arcade: plumber climbs sloped girders and ladders to the top while an ape rolls barrels down. Hero pixel-map poses (≥2 frames): idle, run, climb, jump, hit/fall. Barrels MUST stay on girder yAt(x), roll to the low end, tumble to the next floor, reverse — never free-fall off the first floor. Jump over barrels to score; touch loses a life. Controls: ArrowLeft/Right, ArrowUp/Down climb, Space jump, R restart. Reach top to win. Classic DK colors and silhouettes via pixel maps. On-screen sizes: hero ~48x64, barrels ~32x32, ape ~96x96. imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via canvas fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units. Mario/plumber STARTS on the BOTTOM girder. Girders must SLANT so barrels ROLL downhill then TUMBLE at ladder gaps; ape at the top. TARGET=/640png JMR: ONE 640×480 HTML file. Emit <assets> for STEM-N.png / jmr:spr:N sheets (no sounds/videos tags; no CDN; no WebGL/three.js). imageSmoothingEnabled=false. HUD via fillText. Never ship solid colored squares/circles as the final look for playfield units.
Build a Doom game. 3D first person shooter using three.js from CDN (Scene + PerspectiveCamera + WebGLRenderer — do NOT hand-roll a canvas DDA raycaster): The player walks through a textured maze of walls, floor, and ceiling with mouse-look (pointer-lock) and WASD movement, shooting monsters that approach as billboard sprites always facing the camera. Each monster needs an idle frame and an attack/hit frame; the first-person weapon is a screen-space overlay with idle and muzzle-flash firing frames (the muzzle points UP in the source art). A crosshair sits at screen center and the camera does all the aiming. Controls: WASD move, mouse look, click or Space fire, R restart. Pick up health and ammo; clear all monsters to finish the level, dying at zero health. HUD with health, ammo, score, and a small top-right overview map. Generate VIDEO CUTSCENES for a level-intro establishing shot (corridor or hellscape) and a boss-reveal clip before the final encounter (seeded from key-art stills via image-to-video); muted skippable full-screen overlays, FPS gameplay stays in the three.js scene. High-resolution detailed wall textures and monster sprites, transparent backgrounds on the sprites, plus gunfire/explosion SFX and ominous looping music.
Build a Street Fighter game. a blue-gi player versus a red-gi CPU fighter, always facing each other on a dojo stage. Each fighter is a detailed martial artist that needs animated poses seeded from its idle — idle, walk, jump, crouch/duck, block, punch (arm fully extended, fist forward), kick (leg raised high toward the opponent), throw-fireball (arm thrust forward as a projectile launches), hit/stagger, and a dramatic death/KO fall — at least 2 frames from idle per action so each move reads clearly. Controls: ArrowLeft/Right move, ArrowUp jump, ArrowDown duck, J punch, K kick, L fireball, R restart. A health bar per fighter at the top; punches, kicks, and fireballs drain the opponent's health, and reaching zero triggers the death animation and a round-end screen. The CPU approaches, attacks up close, throws fireballs at range, and jumps or ducks to dodge. Generate VIDEO CUTSCENES for the cinematic beats — a pre-fight intro (both fighters face off in a dojo) and a KO victory clip when a fighter's health hits zero — each seeded from a generated key-art still via image-to-video so the clips match the sprite art; play as muted full-screen overlays any key skips, and the round fight itself stays sprite-animated on the canvas. High-resolution detailed sprites, transparent backgrounds, crisp shading, plus hit sounds and looping fight music. Fighters always face each other. Kick and punch hitboxes must travel toward the opponent — if the player is left of CPU, kick extends with positive horizontal reach toward +x; mirror sprite with scaleX when facing left but do not invert damage direction. Expose facing on state. Movement from crouch must not block arrow keys.
Build a Galaga game. Formation shooter: The player ship at the bottom moves left/right and fires upward. Insect-like enemies fly in along curving paths, assemble into a formation at the top, then peel off in diving attack runs while firing at the player. Enemies have a 2-frame wing-flap animation. Controls: ArrowLeft/Right move, Space fire, R restart. Clear the wave to advance (more enemies, more aggressive dives); being hit by an enemy or its shot loses a life. HUD with score and lives. Crisp colorful high-resolution sprites on a starfield, transparent backgrounds.
Build a Pinball game. A ball falls under gravity and bounces off walls, bumpers, and ramps; two flippers at the bottom (Z and / or Left/Right Shift) bat the ball upward. Bumpers score points and add impulse. Drain between flippers loses the ball; plunger relaunch. HUD: score, balls left. Controls: flipper keys, R restart. Expose window.state.ball and flippers for probes.
